data.label: Amazon's sales since you hit play

notes: Maths: rate = $716,900,000,000 ÷ 31,536,000 s (365 days) = $22,732.75 a second (shown ≈ $22,700). Passes: $65,052 ÷ 22,732.75 = 2.862 s; $393,700 ÷ 22,732.75 = 17.319 s (≈ every 17 s); $650,520 ÷ 22,732.75 = 28.616 s (≈ 29 s). Counter -0.4 to 28.6 s (29.0 s of counting, already running at frame 1; the passes land 0.4 s earlier than the times above): 22,732.75 × 29 = 659,249.75 → ≈ $659,250. Per hour: 22,732.75 × 3,600 = $81,837,900 ≈ $82 million (22,700 × 3,600 = 81,720,000, also ≈ $82 million). Per day: $716.9B ÷ 365 = $1.964B ≈ $2 billion. Median pay = BLS median usual weekly earnings, full-time, Q2 2026: $1,251 × 52 = $65,052; × 10 = $650,520. Sources (as verified in teasers/v2/10-cost-counter.md): Amazon Q4 2025 results (Feb 2026): 2025 net sales $716.9B; BLS USDL-26-1257 (2026-07-21): $1,251 a week; Census/HUD New Residential Sales, Aug 2026 (2026-09-24): median new house $393,700. Sales are seasonal, so this is the year's average rate.
